title: Judicial discretion
summary: Judicial discretion is the authority a rule or doctrine gives a judge to choose among legally permissible responses after considering relevant facts and interests. The authority remains bounded by the governing law.
notes: Discretion is distinct from a party’s contractual power to make performance choices. It also does not mean that a court may disregard mandatory requirements or resolve genuine credibility disputes on summary judgment.

sections.Meaning: Judicial discretion is the authority a rule or doctrine gives a judge to choose among legally permissible responses after considering relevant facts and interests. The authority remains bounded by the governing law.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the decision being entrusted to the judge, the factors the law requires, and the alternatives available. Examples include declining supplemental jurisdiction, transferring a case, managing joined claims, and deciding whether litigation can proceed without an absent person. Explain how the particular facts affect those factors.
